title: Research & Reproduction track
summary: Four capstones that prove you can do credible empirical research: interpret a model mechanistically, run a real causal analysis, design and run an A/B test, and build a domain model end-to-end. The bundle hiring managers read as 'can be trusted with an open research question.'
contentIntro:
## What this track proves

Four capstones, in order:

1. **Mechanistic interpretability: induction heads** — you can open a model and explain a specific circuit
2. **Run a causal analysis** — you can defend a causal claim from non-experimental data
3. **Design and run an A/B test** — you can produce a decision-grade experimental result
4. **Build a protein language model** — you can take a domain problem end-to-end

Each produces an independently-signed public artifact; completing the required set mints a track-level credential.
contentUndergrad:
## What this track proves

The Research & Reproduction track bundles four capstones into one program. It's designed around a single skill: producing empirical results other people can trust.

### The capstones (in order)

1. **[Mechanistic interpretability: induction heads](/capstones/mech-interp-induction-heads)** — locate and characterize an induction circuit, with ablations that isolate it.
2. **[Run a causal analysis](/capstones/run-a-causal-analysis)** — a full observational causal study with a pre-registered DAG, sensitivity analysis, and negative controls.
3. **[Design and run an A/B test](/capstones/design-and-run-an-ab-test)** — power analysis up front, a clean readout, and an honest discussion of what the result does and doesn't support.
4. **[Build a protein language model](/capstones/build-a-protein-language-model)** — a domain modeling project taken from data to evaluation.

Each capstone artifact carries a signed transcript; the chain of trust ends at the published ed25519 key. Self-paced; AI tutoring + peer review + the misconception coach run alongside.
contentGrad:
## What this track proves (for someone reading the artifact)

A learner who completes this track has demonstrated: mechanistic understanding (can isolate and defend a specific model circuit with ablations), causal-inference discipline (pre-registered DAG, sensitivity bounds, negative controls — not just a regression), experimental rigor (power analysis before data, honest null discussion), and the ability to carry a domain modeling problem end-to-end. The defense thread on each artifact covers the specific tradeoffs of that capstone and how the four together evidence research trustworthiness — including what they do not prove.
